q.t: The four angles of a quadrilateral add up to:
q.e: A diagonal cuts it into two triangles, each with 180°.

q.t: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 80°, 90° and 100°. Find the fourth (in degrees).
A quadrilateral with all sides equal and every angle 90° is a:
q.e: A rhombus has equal sides, a rectangle has right angles; a square has both.

q.t: A quadrilateral in which both pairs of opposite sides are parallel is a:
q.e: That is the definition of a parallelogram.

q.t: A kite has:
o: Two pairs of equal adjacent sides
Two pairs of equal opposite sides
q.e: In a kite the equal sides are next to each other, not opposite.

q.t: The diagonals of a rectangle are:
o: Equal, and they bisect each other
Equal but never bisect each other
q.e: ∆ADC ≅ ∆DAB (SAS) gives equal diagonals; another pair of congruent triangles shows they cut each other in half.

q.t: A parallelogram has one angle of 30°. What is the angle next to it (in degrees)?
q.e: Neighbouring angles are co-interior angles between parallel sides, so they add to 180°.

q.t: A trapezium has:
o: At least one pair of parallel sides
Two pairs of parallel sides always
q.e: One pair of parallel opposite sides is enough.

q.t: Can a quadrilateral have three right angles and a fourth angle that is not 90°?
q.e: The angle sum fixes the fourth angle.

q.t: A diagonal of a square splits each corner angle into two angles of:
q.e: The triangle on either side is isosceles (equal sides) with a 90° corner, so its other two angles are equal: 90 ÷ 2 = 45.

q.t: The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5 : 6. Find the largest (in degrees).
q.e: 18 parts make 360°, so one part is 20° and the largest is 120°.

q.t: One angle of a parallelogram is 110°. What are all four angles?
o: 110°, 110°, 70°, 70° in that order round the shape
q.e: Opposite angles are equal and neighbours add to 180°.

q.t: Rhombus ABCD has ∠A = 50°. Find ∠B (in degrees).
q.e: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so neighbouring angles add to 180°.

q.t: The diagonals of a rhombus cross at what angle?
q.e: The two triangles on either side of one diagonal are congruent (SSS), so the angles at the centre are equal and lie on a straight line: 90° each.

q.t: A carpenter's two strips (the diagonals) are 8 cm each, joined at their midpoints at ANY angle. The thread round their ends makes a:
q.e: Equal diagonals that bisect each other always give a rectangle; the crossing angle only changes its shape.

q.t: In trapezium ABCD, AB ∥ DC and ∠B = 85°. Find ∠C (in degrees).
q.e: BC is a transversal of the parallel sides, so ∠B + ∠C = 180°.

q.t: An isosceles trapezium has one angle of 100°. Its angles are:
q.e: Base angles of an isosceles trapezium are equal, and angles along each slanted side add to 180°.

q.t: Two identical equilateral triangles of side 4 cm are joined along a side. The quadrilateral is a:
o: Kite that is not a rhombus
q.e: All four sides are 4 cm; corners are 60° or 60° + 60° = 120°.

q.t: The angles of a quadrilateral are x°, (x + 10)°, (x + 20)° and (x + 30)°. Find x.
Two perpendicular diameters PL and AM of a circle are joined to form APML. It is a:
o: Rhombus that is not a square
Rectangle that is not a square
Kite that is not a rhombus
q.e: Its diagonals are equal (diameters), bisect each other (at the centre) and are at 90°.

q.t: 'A quadrilateral whose diagonals are equal and bisect each other must be a square.' This is:
o: False — it must be a rectangle
False — it must be a kite
False — it must be a trapezium
q.e: Without the 90° crossing it can be any rectangle.

q.t: 'A quadrilateral whose diagonals are perpendicular must be a rhombus.' This is:
o: False — a kite also has perpendicular diagonals
q.e: Perpendicular diagonals alone don't force all sides equal.

q.t: 'A quadrilateral with opposite angles equal must be a parallelogram.' This is:
q.e: Angles x, y, x, y with 2x + 2y = 360 give x + y = 180, so co-interior angles make the sides parallel.

q.t: A quadrilateral has both pairs of opposite sides equal. It must be a:
q.e: Draw a diagonal: SSS gives congruent triangles, so alternate angles are equal and opposite sides are parallel.

q.t: In a rectangle a diagonal makes 30° with the longer side. What angle does it make with the shorter side (in degrees)?
q.e: The two parts of the 90° corner add to 90.

q.t: In a rectangle the diagonals cross at 110°. What is each base angle of the isosceles triangle with the 110° angle at its tip (in degrees)?
q.e: Half-diagonals are equal, so the triangle is isosceles: (180 − 110) ÷ 2 = 35.

q.t: In kite ABCD, AB = AD and CB = CD. ∠B = 110° and ∠A = 60°. Find ∠C (in degrees).
q.e: The kite is symmetric about AC, so ∠D = ∠B = 110°. Then ∠C = 360 − 220 − 60 = 80.

q.t: Two identical scalene triangles (6, 9, 12 cm) are joined on the 12 cm side by FLIPPING one over. The result is a:
q.e: Flipping puts equal sides next to each other — adjacent equal pairs make a kite. Turning 180° would give a parallelogram.

q.t: Which quadrilateral is both a kite and a rectangle?
q.e: A rectangle's adjacent sides must then be equal, which makes all sides equal: a square.

q.t: In trapezium ABCD, AB ∥ DC and ∠A : ∠D = 2 : 3. Find ∠D (in degrees).
q.e: ∠A + ∠D = 180° (co-interior). 5 parts → 36° each, so ∠D = 108°.

q.t: U, V, W, X are the midpoints of the sides of square CASE. Quadrilateral UVWX is a:
o: Rhombus that is not a square
Rectangle that is not a square
Kite that is not a rhombus
q.e: The four corner triangles are congruent isosceles right triangles, giving equal sides, and 45° + 90° + 45° = 180° at each midpoint gives right angles.

q.t: A quadrilateral has four equal sides and one 90° angle. It is a:
o: Rhombus that is not a square
q.e: It's a rhombus (a parallelogram); neighbours add to 180°, so every angle is 90°.

q.t: In quadrilateral ABCD, ∠A + ∠B = 220°. The bisectors of ∠C and ∠D meet at O. Find ∠COD (in degrees).
q.e: ∠C + ∠D = 140°, halves add to 70°, so ∠COD = 180 − 70 = 110°.

q.t: The bisectors of the four angles of a parallelogram (not a rhombus) enclose a:
q.e: Adjacent angles add to 180°, so their halves add to 90° and the bisectors meet at right angles.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = (3x + 10)° and ∠B = (2x + 20)°. Find ∠C (in degrees).
A geoboard square's diagonals are equal and perpendicular. One diagonal is now extended 2 cm at each end. The shape becomes a:
o: Kite that is not a rhombus
q.e: Diagonals still bisect each other at 90° but are no longer equal.

q.t: Why are the diagonals of a parallelogram usually NOT equal?
o: Equal diagonals would force all angles to 90° — a rectangle
q.e: Equal diagonals that bisect each other is the rectangle's special property.

q.t: The four angles of a quadrilateral are consecutive multiples of 12. Find the largest (in degrees).
A concave ('dented') quadrilateral's angles add up to:
q.e: The diagonal from the dented corner lies inside and makes two triangles: 180° + 180°.

q.t: In a kite ABCD (AB = BC, CD = DA), the diagonal BD:
q.e: ∆ABD ≅ ∆CBD (SSS) then ∆AOB ≅ ∆COB (SAS) give AO = OC and equal angles at O on a straight line, so 90°.
